rows.note: tests/browser/resilience.spec.ts:75 does not test a cancelled drag. It dispatches synthetic touch events with pointerId 7. controller.ts:548 calls setPointerCapture before p.begin() at :549, and Chrome throws NotFoundError for a pointer id that is not active. So begin() never runs, pointermove is ignored (dragging false), and pointercancel ends a drag that never started. The test passes whatever the cancel path does. The cancel wiring is therefore covered only by code reading, plus the sibling mouse-release test. A fix would use a real touch or mouse drag (page.touchscreen, or CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent with a cancel), or would call begin() before setPointerCapture. rows.evidence: Implementation: controller.ts:569-572 and :587-592 route pointercancel and lostpointercapture to endPointer(true), then scene.pointer.end, then Business release() (src/scenes/business/index.ts:282). Test: tests/browser/resilience.spec.ts:75-90 dispatches synthetic touch events with pointerId 7. Probe in this audit (scratchpad/skeptic-m4/capture-probe.mjs, installed Chrome 154.0.8037.58): setPointerCapture on a dispatched pointerId 7 throws 'NotFoundError: No active pointer with the given id is found', while a real mouse pointer (id 1) is captured (has=true). In the controller that throw happens at controller.ts:548, before p.begin at :549. The drag therefore never starts, and Business move() returns at once while not dragging (business/index.ts:267). Related: business.spec.ts:89 (in the checkpoint-3 33/33 run) covers release() after a real mouse drag ended by pointerup.
rows.note: The spec only shows that a pointercancel during the approach sends no request and the scan completes. No drag is in progress when the cancel arrives, and the page throws an uncaught NotFoundError that the test does not listen for. The code path is shared: pointercancel reaches the same release() as pointerup, which business.spec.ts:89 exercises. Still, no check cancels an active drag. To close it, cancel a real touch drag: use CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent (touchStart, touchMove, touchCancel) or a hasTouch context, assert the card is displaced before the cancel, and fail on pageerror. No physical-device run exists. (skeptic: The cited test does not exercise a cancelled drag: measured, setPointerCapture throws for its synthetic pointer before the drag begins.)

The record shadow has no tight line layer (models/recordPlayer.ts:47-50). No test or measurement covers it. This review measured outputs/party/frames-host (11:34). The strip of deck just in front of the platter keeps a mean luminance of 229.1–229.4 from f0000 (hover) to f0090 (seated). Elsewhere the shadow falls on the near-black rubber mat (mat_rubber, models/recordPremium.ts:219-227), and no tightening is visible in the f0018–f0075 crops.
rows.note: The settle half is met. The shadow tightening is implemented but unchecked, and the captures do not show it. The checkpoint-3 approval was for the whole scene (docs/style-reference.md:28) and records nothing about this beat. It needs a targeted check, for example a still diff of the shadow layer at h≈0.3 against contact, or Surya's confirmation that the look is acceptable. pendingOn: measurements or surya. (skeptic: 'met' requires a check. The auditor's own note says no automated check exists. The recorded review is generic, and this review's measurement of the host frames finds no visible tightening.)

The first frames of outputs/party/_strip-decline.png (checkpoint 3) show the parked arm.
rows.note: A cp4 motion finding said this 0.20 s hold reads as dead time after an interruption blend (motion-party-change-dead-hold). The verifier rejected it because the hold is this beat.

rows.requirement: 0.20-1.00 s: lid closes on its actual hinge; acceleration and braking suggest a light damped mechanism
rows.evidence: sequences.ts:109-121 uses a Beta(2, 4.5) CDF: one speed peak, then braking, leaving about 0.93° of travel after 1.00 s. tests/party.test.ts:122 'the lid closes on its hinge without passing closed, braking into a soft close' passes; it checks the close is monotonic, has a single peak, and is slower late than mid-swing. Clip: outputs/party/decline.mp4 (11:34).

rows.requirement: 1.00-1.40 s: gentle contact and settle; no slam or negative sound
rows.evidence: The lid makes contact at 1.30 s at zero speed and then holds (sequences.ts:115-119; tests/party.test.ts:145-146). There is no audio (docs/asset-manifest.md:57). The final frames of outputs/party/_strip-decline.png are static.

rows.requirement: If changing from an accepted state, the shared reset first restores tonearm and record-ready pose before decline
rows.evidence: Recorded deviation: docs/spec-revisions.md:16 (#10 'Tonearm reversal': an arm lift step of about 0.5° in one frame, recorded at checkpoint 3) and docs/qualification.md:154. Implementation: Party has no interruptCut, so a change blends through guest-ready over INTERRUPT_BLEND = 150 ms before decline starts (src/core/visualDirector.ts:11, 141-157, 199). PartyScene.refresh derives the arm lift from yaw (src/scenes/party/index.ts:52-56; sequences.ts:131-136). tests/party.test.ts:290 'an interruption during the arm lift never drops the arm in one frame, and never drags it' passes. Browser check: party.spec.ts:99. In the cp4 technical matrix (cp4/technical/phaseC-party.json), accept→decline at 80, 480, 880, 1280 and 1552 ms all end exactly on the canonical declined still.
rows.note: Open cp4 polish finding motion-interrupt-blend-quality (confirmed): the quaternion blend turns the record and platter by the shortest path. The label therefore spins backwards about 43° on a change at 0.5 s, and about 51.6° from the settled accepted pose (outputs/party/frames-change f0030–f0039). The change clip still interrupts at 0.5 s (scripts/capture.ts:257), so no capture shows the settled accepted-pose → decline path.

rows.requirement: The lid must never pass through the tonearm or record
rows.evidence: tests/party.test.ts:231 sweeps the built lid shell through 133 angles over the guest-ready platter, record and arm, sampled at <=1 cm, and requires 0 cuts. It also checks host-ready and accepted. :215 checks clearance with the lid closed. Both pass at HEAD. The interruption blend keeps the lid open, since both endpoints use LID_OPEN. Decline always starts from guest-ready (src/core/visualDirector.ts:137-138, 199, 232-236).

rows.requirement: Authored: record placement, tonearm, spindle rotation, lid travel, shadows
rows.evidence: All of these are pure functions of time (src/scenes/party/sequences.ts:8-12, 56-121). The shadows derive from the authored record height (src/scenes/party/index.ts:85, 88-91). The 1 ms sampling tests in tests/party.test.ts:36-147 check them and pass.

rows.requirement: Optional spring: no more than 1° lid settling at the end; skip it if it looks like a bounce

rows.requirement: Do not simulate the hinge or let physics determine whether the lid closes
rows.evidence: A grep of src/scenes/party, models/recordPlayer.ts and models/recordContract.ts finds no spring, stepper or physics. The lid angle is lerp(LID_OPEN, LID_CLOSED, CLOSE(t)) (sequences.ts:119). Covered by tests/party.test.ts:122.

rows.requirement: Clock-driven rotation must be invariant to frame rate
rows.evidence: spin = SPIN.total * spinProgress(t), an absolute function of t (sequences.ts:101-104). Two shared tests pass at HEAD: tests/visual-director.test.ts:154 'sequences are frame-rate invariant: same pose at the same active time' (30 vs 120 fps) and tests/clock.test.ts:18 (hidden-tab pause). In the cp4 technical review, hiding the tab mid-decline ran no frames, and the 1400 ms sequence took 1423 ms of active time (cp4/technical/phaseF.json party).

rows.requirement: Ready: open lid, record seated, arm parked
